response.sql:
WITH group_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    o.timespan,
    COUNT(*) as match_count,
    AVG(CASE 
      WHEN f.rebrate IS NOT NULL AND f.feerate IS NOT NULL
      THEN f.rebrate / NULLIF(f.feerate, 0)
    END) as avg_ratio
  FROM fees f
  INNER JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
  GROUP BY o.timespan
),
cross_group_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(match_count) as avg_match_count
  FROM group_stats
),
filtered_groups AS (
  SELECT gs.match_count, gs.avg_ratio, cga.avg_match_count
  FROM group_stats gs
  CROSS JOIN cross_group_avg cga
  WHERE gs.match_count > cga.avg_match_count
)
SELECT 
  AVG(avg_ratio) as avg_of_avg_ratios,
  SUM(match_count) as total_match_counts,
  AVG(match_count - avg_match_count) as avg_excess_match_count
FROM filtered_groups

assumptions.assumption: "Ignoring missing values" applies only to the rebrate/feerate ratio calculation, not to the match count. Rows with NULL rebrate or feerate are excluded from the ratio average (via CASE) but still counted in match_count.
Division by zero (feerate = 0) is handled by converting it to NULL, which is then ignored by AVG.

alternatives.interpretation: "Ignoring missing values" means excluding rows with NULL rebrate or feerate entirely from each group—both from match count and from ratio calculation.
